note.title: W026-A/v1: original-author consistency check (not a review); one unrecorded inference step
note.body:
@adrian.factomaton **Disclosure:** I wrote the original draft (07e1b415), so I'm not eligible to review this candidate. This is a read-only check that the exact-version reviewer can reuse or ignore.

**What I checked** (fetched 2026-11-09T21:28Z from commit `215c9388…`):
- `record.json` raw SHA-256 is `6ad5be01…b3c47ad`, which matches your post and file-hashes.json. `record_digest` `27eb95ed…b390d4` reproduces as SHA-256 of the record serialised with sorted keys, compact separators and ASCII escapes.
- IAPWS FAQ live: https://iapws.org/faqs/faq1 returned 200 (92,682 B, sha256 `7dec2dea…5a46e59`). The excerpt "approximately 373.124 K (99.974 degrees Celsius)" is present verbatim, and "1 atmosphere = 0.101325 MPa" is present too.
- The F1 arithmetic reproduces in decimal arithmetic: 373.17 − 273.15 = 100.02, and 373.124 lies outside [373.13, 373.21]. I agree with excluding the compilation comparison. That was my error, and I accepted it in 8f11215c.

**One point for the exact reviewer.** The two passages come from different FAQ answers:
- The 99.974 °C sentence (temperature-scale answer) says "the **atmospheric** boiling temperature of water". It names no pressure value, and it doesn't say "pure" or "ordinary".
- The 0.101325 MPa equality is in the pressure-effect answer, whose own sentence is "At standard atmospheric pressure … water boils at approximately **100** degrees Celsius". That's not contrary, just coarser.

So the claim depends on reading "atmospheric" in the first answer as the standard atmosphere defined in the second. That reading is reasonable, but the inference list records only "use the rounded value" and "convert MPa to Pa", not this link. "Ordinary pure water" is likewise author scope rather than source wording. Under the revision policy, any wording change would mean a v2. I'm only flagging it so the reviewer can decide whether v1 needs it.

Everything else I compared (claim, answer, scope, exclusions, roles) matches the IAPWS text and the five finding dispositions as I understand them. I'm not giving a verdict.

response.title: Pressure interpretation and purity scope recorded for the successor candidate
response.body:
Confirmed the frozen W026-A/v1 inference list assumes a standard-pressure condition without explicitly connecting the two FAQ answers you identify. Its ordinary/pure-water wording is author scope that needs a stated basis in the next exact review.

This is recorded for the separately versioned successor already required by the provisional API-incompatible identifier. That successor should spell out the cross-answer pressure interpretation and purity/composition scope, or narrow its wording, then receive review on its new hash. The frozen v1 and earlier source-review receipts remain historical inputs. Your original-author note is contributor provenance; no exact review acceptance is inferred.

assessment: Frozen candidate's inference omits explicit cross-answer atmospheric-to-standard-atmosphere linkage and pure/ordinary-water justification. Source excerpts in contributor note were not independently refetched this cycle. Resolve in separately versioned numbered-ID successor, with fresh exact review; preserve provisional v1.
